extracted.intended_audience: general public, students, academics and journalists interested in academic integrity and Serbian politics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and summarizing standards, procedures and evaluative principles used by universities and oversight bodies to judge doctoral theses and plagiarism cases, as illustrated by the Siniša Mali scandal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of plagiarism (University of Belgrade Professional Code of Ethics, Art. 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Plagiarism is representation of someone else's ideas or works, entirely or partially, without naming the original authorship or sources, that is, illegal claiming of others intellectual works and scientific results and their representation as your own, so as literal taking of other author's text, that is, copying from electronic and printed sources, from Serbian or foreign language, partially or entirely, without naming author's name and source from which the text was taken, so as without strict marking of the taken part."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formal wording used by the University of Belgrade to classify conduct as plagiarism; it emphasizes literal transcription and copying without attribution across languages and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication/indexing requirement for doctoral submissions (SCIndeks requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code on Accreditation of the Study Programs stipulates that, in order to be accepted for the doctoral theses, work must be published in magazines listed at SCIndeks (Serbian citation-index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if articles used to qualify a candidate are not plagiarized, they are unacceptable for doctoral qualification if they are not published in SCIndeks-listed journals. The article cites this requirement in criticism of Mali's qualifying publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting the same thesis to two faculties
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting one the same thesis at two faculties is forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The controversy over Mali switching faculties (Faculty of Economics → Faculty of Organizational Sciences) turned on whether the accepted dissertation was the same work rejected earlier; this prohibition is a procedural rule relevant to validity of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissions must check originality, not judge scientific contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: University Professional Ethics Board concluded that the faculty's commission 'didn't check if the doctorate is plagiarized at all, judging the “scientific contribution” instead, which wasn't its task.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigatory bodies are expected to determine whether a work is original (i.e., free from plagiarism) rather than evaluate its scientific contribution when handling plagiarism complaints; conflating the two is a procedural error that can invalidate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism-detection software is a tool, not sole basis for proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty commissions repeatedly stated 'software checks can't be the basis for the proceedings' and the Professional Ethics Board instructed that software check is only one of the ways to check for plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated similarity reports (e.g., Turnitin) can help detect overlaps but must be supplemented by manual expert review, especially for translation-based copying or contextual assessment; software limitations should be explicitly acknowledged in procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of automated tools for cross-language/translation plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts and critics noted that Turnitin (and similar tools) can't reliably compare theses in two different languages and that translation plagiarism must be checked 'by hand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where suspected copying involves translation from another language, manual, expert linguistic comparison is required because similarity-detection software may miss literal translations or misclassify common phrases and formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed percentage cutoff; context matters (debate over quantitative thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Experts Commission reported that Mali plagiarized 6.97% (or 16% by another count) and concluded this was 'not enough to dispute its scientific contribution', while critics argued 'you can't plagiarize a little' and that percentage thresholds are misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should not rely solely on arbitrary percent thresholds; evaluators must consider nature, location, and significance of copied passages (entire passages/pages vs. incidental phrasing), and institutional rules should clarify how quantitative measures are interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissions' composition and conflict-of-interest standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism focused on commissions lacking subject-matter expertise, containing members with conflicts (mentors, editors, co-authors), or members unable to assess sources (language gaps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigatory panels should be impartial and include experts in the thesis subject and relevant languages; conflicts of interest (e.g., mentors, co-authors, editors of qualifying journals) must be avoided to ensure legitimacy of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of government/state documents in thesis is not automatically mitigating
rubrics_metrics.description: The Experts Commission treated copying from official state reports and government publications as partly explaining overlap, whereas critics noted that in other jurisdictions (e.g., Germany) misuse of state resources can be an aggravating circumstance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should specify how use of state-produced material is treated: whether it can mitigate or aggravate plagiarism findings, and whether permission/citation norms differ for public reports versus copyrighted academic works.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statute of limitations for plagiarism (institutional stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rector stated that 'plagiarati ne mogu da zastare' (plagiarism cannot become time-barred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities may treat plagiarism as actionable regardless of how much time has passed since the degree was awarded; institutional policies should state whether and how historical cases are investigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper evidentiary standards in plagiarism complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints and appeals criticized commissions for selective citation of pages and incomplete evidence; the Professional Ethics Board returned reports as 'incomplete, unclear and contradictory.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should assemble comprehensive, transparent evidence (full comparisons, page-by-page citations, illustrations) and explain methodology; selective or cursory treatment undermines trust and may require rehearing.
